S81.01.note: The recorded catalog version has no visible screen. The resolver is apps/web/lib/services/entitlement-resolution.ts.
steps: Open the Pricing page at /pricing (the Pricing link in the marketing header, or Compare plans on Settings > Billing for a Free account).
Read the monthly prices on the Basic, Premium, Max and Ultra cards.
Compare with Expected: prices should come from the one billing catalog. No screen I found shows the catalog version a subscription was sold under.

Open Settings > Usage and read the card "Upgrade for higher capacity" (a Free account sees only the Upgrade button, no meters).
Open the Pricing page at /pricing and scroll to "Compare plans".
Read the Free column and compare it with Expected: the Free bundle should be listed, and the same limits should be what the app enforces.

S81.07.note: The multiplier text is a template filled at render; I did not render the live card, so the exact numbers are from code, not the screen.
steps: Open the Pricing page at /pricing.
Read the usage sentence on the Max card and on the Ultra card.
Read the Premium card to see what it is measured against.

Compare with Expected: the page should say what 1x means. Code shows no separate 1x plan: each multiplier names its baseline (Max and Ultra against Premium, Premium against Basic). Code computes Max as 5x Premium on every window, and Ultra as 10x Premium on weekly and monthly with no five-hour cap, so Ultra will not read 15x.
S81.07.where: Pricing page > usage sentence on the Max card and the Ultra card

S81.08.needs: a paid account for Settings > Usage bars (a Free account sees the Upgrade card)
S81.08.note: When all windows share one multiplier, the copy says only "more usage" and does not name a window; the monthly window is not named in any multiplier line.
steps: Open the Pricing page at /pricing and read the usage sentence on the Max card.
Open Settings > Usage and find the card "Plan usage limits".
Read which bars appear: "Current session", "This week" and "Most capable models".
Compare with Expected: the multiplier should name the allowance it scales (session, weekly or monthly).
S81.08.where: Pricing page > usage sentence on the Max card, and Settings > Usage > Plan usage limits

S81.09.needs: a Free or Basic account for the gate test
S81.09.note: Rows come from the capability table; the server-side gate per capability is not visible in the UI.
steps: Open the Pricing page at /pricing and scroll to "Compare plans".
Read the capability rows (for example "Cloud API access") across Free, Basic, Premium, Max and Ultra.
Compare with Expected: each plan's feature differences should be listed.
Test one gate: on a Free or Basic account open Settings > Account > API keys and see whether the plan gate appears.

labels.text: Drop a file here or click to upload

S81.11.needs: a Free account and a file larger than the remaining storage
S81.11.note: The Free limit is 500 MB in billing-catalog.ts. The exact trigger text for Project settings was not confirmed. The error message is built in apps/web/lib/services/free-plan-entitlements.ts.
steps: Sign in with a Free account and open Projects from the sidebar, then open a project.
Open Project settings and scroll to the "Files" heading.
Read the storage line "X of Y storage" if it appears.
Upload a file larger than the remaining space and read the error: "accounts include ... of file storage, shared by your Library and project sources".
Compare with Expected: the limit shown should match the plan's storage limit.
S81.11.where: Projects > open a project > Project settings > Files

Read the "Context window" row across the plans, for example "Up to N tokens".
Compare with Expected: each plan should show its own context size.
S81.12.where: Pricing page > Compare plans > Context window row

Look for the refusal "Your plan allows ... response at a time" on the third chat.

In the composer footer, click the control labelled "Reasoning effort".
Look for locked effort levels marked "Upgrade" and the link "What each plan includes".
Open the model picker and look for locked models showing "<plan> and above".
Compare with Expected: gated options should be shown and blocked by plan.

S81.15.needs: a paid account (the bar appears only when the plan has a flagship weekly cap)
S81.15.note: Admission enforcement is in apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-request-service.ts; the bar is hidden when there is no flagship cap.

Find the card "Plan usage limits".
Read the bar "Most capable models" and its reset time.
Compare with Expected: the flagship cap should show and be enforced on admission.

Switch to the business audience and find the Team Premium card.
Read "Higher usage than a Standard seat" and the per-seat usage text ("for every seat").

S81.17.needs: none to read; do not complete checkout
S81.17.note: Only Team and Team Premium have yearly prices in billing-catalog.ts.
steps: Open the Pricing page at /pricing and switch to the business audience.
On the Team card, find the cadence group "Team billing cadence" with "Monthly" and "Annual".
Click "Annual" and read "save N% annually" and the new per-seat price.
Open checkout only to read the charge, and stop before paying.
Compare with Expected: the saving and the billing cadence should match. Individual plans offer monthly only.
S81.17.where: Pricing page > Team card > Monthly / Annual toggle

S81.18.needs: an account with an active trial
S81.18.note: No plan in billing-catalog.ts has a trialDays value. Trials come from referral trial days (apps/web/lib/services/referral-service.ts). I did not find a control that starts a trial directly.
steps: Sign in with an account that has a trial (granted through a referral).
Open Settings > Billing.
Read the status "Free trial" and the row "Trial ends on".
Compare with Expected: the trial should be shown as a trial and end on that date.
S81.18.where: Settings > Billing (status "Free trial" and "Trial ends on")

S81.19.needs: a paid-eligible account and a promotion code
S81.19.note: The account menu trigger text was not confirmed; the menu item "Upgrade" is in apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountMenuItems.tsx.
steps: Open the account menu and click "Upgrade". Choose a plan.
In the upgrade confirm step, find the field labelled "Promotion code" (shown only when an amount is due).
Enter a valid promotion code and read the discount line.
Open Settings > Usage and read "Bonus credits" under "Credit balances".
Compare with Expected: the promotion should apply to the account and be visible.
S81.19.where: Account menu > Upgrade > choose a plan > Promotion code field; and Settings > Usage > Credit balances > Bonus credits

S81.20.needs: a Free or paid account; a payment method to complete a purchase
steps: Open Settings > Billing and scroll to the credit pack panel.
Choose a pack or type an amount in "Other amount".
Click "Buy credits" and stop at checkout (do not pay unless intended).
After a completed purchase, open Settings > Usage and read "Purchased credits" apart from the plan allowance.
Compare with Expected: the purchased balance should carry over and show separately.
S81.20.where: Settings > Billing > "Buy credits" panel, then Settings > Usage > Credit balances > Purchased credits

labels.text: Keep going after a usage limit

S81.21.needs: a paid account with purchased credits
S81.21.note: The switch appears only when the account can buy top-ups. Separate accounting was not confirmed on screen.
steps: Sign in with a paid account billed through Stripe, Apple or Google, and open Settings > Billing.
Find the switch "Keep going after a usage limit" (off by default).
Read the text: "Spend your credits when a usage limit stops you" with the available credit amount, or "Buy credits above to use this."
Turn the switch on and check that it stays on after a reload.
Compare with Expected: overage should be opt-in and accounted separately from the plan windows.
S81.21.where: Settings > Billing > "Keep going after a usage limit" switch

S81.22.needs: a subscriber on a retired plan (not available in a normal test account)
S81.22.note: No retired-plan screen found. Version tables in packages/contracts/types/src/managed-usage-limits.ts currently map every version to the same limits, so no difference is visible today.

S81.23.needs: a paid or Free account; do not confirm the charge
S81.23.note: The dialog states the charge today but I did not find text giving the exact effective time.
steps: Open Settings > Billing and click "Adjust plan" (or "Upgrade plan" on a Free account).
Choose a higher plan.
In the dialog "Upgrade to {planLabel}", read the line "You'll be charged ... today. After that, ... renews at ..." and the "Plan summary".
Compare with Expected: the charge, the new renewal date and the effective time should be shown before confirming. Do not click "Confirm" unless you intend to pay.
S81.23.where: Settings > Billing > "Adjust plan" (or "Upgrade plan" on Free), then choose a higher plan and the "Upgrade to {planLabel}" dialog

labels.text: at the end of your current billing period

S81.24.needs: a paid Stripe account with a smaller plan available
steps: Sign in with a paid account billed through Stripe and open Settings > Billing.
Click "Switch to a smaller plan" (shown only when no downgrade is already scheduled).
Read the dialog: the smaller plan starts "at the end of your current billing period" with the date, and "nothing is charged today".
Compare with Expected: the effective time and access kept until then should match. Close the dialog without confirming unless you intend it.
S81.24.where: Settings > Billing > "Switch to a smaller plan"

labels.text: Self-serve plans have no grace period

S81.25.needs: an account with a failed renewal
S81.25.note: Expected asks for a grace rule; the code defines none (paid features stop at the first failed renewal).
steps: Use an account whose last renewal payment failed (a test setup you own), and open Settings > Billing.
Read the notice "Your last ... payment didn't go through, so the plan is past due" or "unpaid".
Read the sentence "Self-serve plans have no grace period" and the action "Update payment method".
Compare with Expected: the access that remains and the fix should be stated. Code states no grace period.
S81.25.where: Settings > Billing (notice after a failed renewal)

S81.26.needs: a Free account and a Premium or higher account
S81.26.note: Gate is managed_api (Premium and above) in billing-catalog.ts; the API route returns managed_api_plan_required.
steps: Sign in with a Free account, open Settings > Account and find "API keys".
Try to create a key and read the upgrade message (plan gate).
Sign in with a Premium or higher account and repeat; a key can now be created.
Open the Pricing page at /pricing and read the "Cloud API access" row in Compare plans.
Compare with Expected: API use should be a plan capability and be blocked without it.
S81.26.where: Settings > Account > "API keys"; Pricing page > Compare plans > "Cloud API access"

S81.27.needs: a paid account and a Free account, both signed in on the web and the desktop app
S81.27.note: The server-side per-surface enforcement is inner behaviour with no control of its own; the tester can only see it by comparing the plan shown on two surfaces. The desktop app shows the hosted web app, so the Billing pane is the same screen there. The surface mapping is in apps/web/lib/free-chat-surface-policy.ts (web, mobile, desktop and chrome map to managed_chat), and the quoted code at BillingSection.tsx:671 has moved, so the exact line was not confirmed.
steps: Sign in to the web app and the AGI Desktop app with the same account.
Open Settings, then click Billing in the left list.
Note the plan name and the Billing page heading on the web.
Repeat on the desktop app and compare: the same plan should show on both.
Optionally, try a paid-only chat option on each surface and compare whether it is allowed the same way.
S81.27.where: Settings > Billing, comparing the plan name shown there on each signed-in surface (web browser and the desktop app)

S81.28.note: The Upgrade page and its copy were confirmed in UpgradeChooser.tsx. The quoted code at apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:223 and plan-display.ts:36 has moved and was not confirmed as the explanation source.
steps: Sign in with a Free account and open a chat.
Click the Upgrade label on a locked option in the chat composer.
On the Upgrade page, look for the Recommended card and the What changes list under it.
Read the Or jump ahead links for the other plans and check that each plan explains what it adds over the current plan.
Compare with Expected: each plan should say what it adds and why the blocked feature needs it.
